description: The working agreement every owned repository is supposed to follow, checked rather than remembered. All of it is written down already; none of it was ever verified by anything, which is how a repository ends up half set up and looking finished.

gates.title: develop Exists
gates.rule: The repository has a develop branch. Without it every branch is cut from main, and a branch cut from main is missing whatever develop already holds.
gates.fix: Create it from the tip of the default branch.

gates.title: Both Branches Are Protected And Gate On check
gates.rule: main and develop both require the check status, refuse force pushes and deletions, and require conversations resolved. develop is strict so a branch is tested against what it will land on; main is not, because a merge-commit promotion leaves develop behind by a commit carrying no code.
gates.fix: Apply the standard protection rule to both branches.

gates.title: Auto-Merge And Branch Deletion Are On
gates.rule: allow_auto_merge and delete_branch_on_merge are both enabled. Without the first nothing lands on its own when CI goes green; without the second every merged branch stays behind forever.
gates.fix: gh api -X PATCH repos/{owner}/{repo} -f allow_auto_merge=true -f delete_branch_on_merge=true

gates.title: The Standard Workflow Is On Both Branches
gates.rule: ci.yml matches the standard byte for byte on main and on develop. A workflow that drifted on one branch gates nothing on that branch, and the branch it gates is not the one anybody looks at.
gates.fix: Write the standard workflow to both branches through the contents API.

gates.title: One README, At The Root
gates.rule: Exactly one README.md exists and it is at the project root. A README in a subdirectory is a second source of truth that goes stale without anybody noticing it exists.
gates.fix: Fold the subdirectory READMEs into the root one and delete them.

gates.title: This Repository Is Held Once On This Machine
gates.rule: No second checkout of the same repository exists. Two checkouts is how a build from the stale twin overwrote a night of work, and the twin looks exactly like the real one until it does.
gates.fix: The gate names them. Keep one, and cut worktrees from it.

gates.title: The Work Is In A Worktree
gates.rule: The changes are in a worktree cut from develop, not in the primary checkout. Two agents in one checkout share a HEAD and an index, and the second to switch branches carries the first one's uncommitted work away.
gates.fix: git worktree add <path> -b <slug> origin/develop, and move the work there.

gates.title: The Branch Is Based On develop
gates.rule: The working branch has origin/develop as an ancestor. A branch cut from main looks fine until its pull request reintroduces already-merged commits or conflicts on files develop has since changed.
gates.fix: Rebase onto origin/develop, or reset onto it and reapply the working changes.
